2e21dde48be974440193a00e7b6441e6a9ca1b9a.summary: Part 1 of an analysis of Panda Banker, a banking trojan that shares some code with the older Zeus malware. It injects code into web browsers to steal banking and card credentials, uses anti-analysis and obfuscation, and deletes itself when monitoring tools are detected. After execution it spawns a second binary. Part 1 covers initial memory analysis of that activity. Behavioural and reverse engineering are deferred to part 2. Published 2021-08-26 by Crovax.

2e9f7dc10f8b0ceb48f5ae3fa136f59af20e7536.summary: Trend Micro report on the Clop ransomware gang. It covers the group's extortion-focused operations, its links to TA505 and FIN7, zero-day exploitation of file transfer software (Kiteworks, GoAnywhere, MOVEit), and 2021 and 2023 ransom and victim statistics, including detection counts by country and sector.

hedges: Although Clop ransomware actors did not share specific details on how they exploited the vulnerability, a researcher published proof-of-concept code and Fortra released an emergency patch.
Microsoft attributed the exploitation of CVE-2023-27350 to the Clop and LockBit gangs, according to the report.
In May of this year, it was reported that FIN7 used the POWERTRASH malware, citing news reporting.
Researchers and analysts have noted that no ransomware payloads were observed from the MOVEit attacks, though the group focused on extortion.
Victim figures come from the leak site and Trend Micro's OSINT research, covering organizations that had refused to pay as of writing.
